insight: The InboundGroupSessionData interface changed between matrix-js-sdk v34 and v38. The old version had `session_id`, `session_key`, `sender_key`, `forwarding_curve25519_key_chain`, and `keys_claimed` fields. The v38 version has `room_id`, `session`, `forwardingCurve25519KeyChain`, `keysClaimed?`, `untrusted?`, and `sharedHistory?` fields. The test data had to be updated to match the new shape.

matrix-js-sdk@38 on Node aborts (WASM `RuntimeError: unreachable`, exit 1) when `client.initRustCrypto()` is called with the SDK default `useIndexedDB:true`, because Node has no `indexedDB` global. This is a hard WASM abort, NOT a catchable JS exception: `try`/`catch`, `--unhandled-rejections`, and `NODE_OPTIONS` all fail to stop it. The fix is prevention, not handling: call `initRustCrypto({ useIndexedDB: false })` (in-memory store; works on Node but keys are NOT durable) and only when E2EE is explicitly opted in (`adapter.json encryption: true`, default false). Also: `createClient({ cryptoStore })` is legacy-crypto/migration-only in v38 — it does NOT persist Rust-crypto E2EE keys, so `SqliteCryptoStore` + `dataPath` does not make E2EE keys survive restart. Verified against the installed SDK (client.d.ts:91-96, 1104; client.js:1087).

DRONE-GW-BUG-002: a persistent Matrix sync store must ACCUMULATE /sync responses, not store the last one. A /sync response is a delta (the first carries room state, later ones carry only next_batch), so `INSERT OR REPLACE` of the last response leaves a valid token with no `rooms` — the client then resumes an incremental sync, getRooms() is empty, and replies fail with "unknown conversation" (persistence becomes WORSE than no store, which would full-sync). Fix mirrors matrix-js-sdk's IndexedDB backend: hold a `SyncAccumulator`, persist `getJSON(true)` (accumulated), return `getJSON()`/`getNextBatchToken()` from it, and rehydrate by replaying persisted state through `accumulate(..., fromDatabase=true)`. Note the gateway's `SqliteSyncStore` reads the DB directly (it never awaited `store.startup()`), so hydration must be lazy; also `createClient({cryptoStore})` being legacy-only (BUG-001) means the sync store and crypto store are independent.

drone-gateway Matrix adapter follow-on (after the sync-store accumulation fix): with a persistent sync store, matrix-js-sdk replays the cached /sync on restart and re-emits every cached timeline event as `RoomEvent.Timeline`. `EventTimelineSet.addLiveEvent` ALWAYS passes `toStartOfTimeline === false`, so `toStartOfTimeline` does NOT distinguish replayed history. The only discriminator is `data.liveEvent` (false when the event came `fromCache`). The adapter filtered on `toStartOfTimeline` alone, so on each restart it re-dispatched historical commands as fresh input — an earlier command's reply then "answered" a later unrelated command, and command replies duplicated once per restart. Fix: take the full 5-arg `RoomEvent.Timeline` signature `(event, room, toStartOfTimeline, removed, data)` and return early on `removed || !data?.liveEvent` (this is the SDK's own documented check, per event-timeline-set docs). Rule: with a persistent store, treat `RoomEvent.Timeline` as "timeline changed", not "new message".

Gateway control surfaces are instantiated per conversation but the engine dispatches messages fire-and-forget (`adapter.onMessage(msg => { void this.handleMessage(msg) })`), so two messages in one conversation run concurrently. Any surface that holds session state (persona-assignment) therefore has a check-then-await-then-set double-spawn race, and LocalSpawnBackend.sendMessage opens a fresh readline over the persistent child stdout on every call, so concurrent readers corrupt each other's output stream. Fix pattern: serialize dispatch per conversation in the engine (promise-chain tail on the instantiated-conversation record), plus in-flight promise caching in both spawn backends — the same queue-if-in-flight mutex used for `_runtime.submitUserMessage` (ADR 198).

When a `apply_diff` hunk's change zone contains template-literal lines (e.g. `` order.push(`start:${text}`) ``), the whitespace-fuzz matcher can collapse the surrounding newlines and silently mangle the file tail (it swallowed an entire `describe` block and the outer close brace in test/engine.test.ts, producing an "Unexpected end of file" from esbuild). The build/test gate caught it, but the reliable fix is: truncate the file at the last known-good line with `head -n N` and re-append the new tail via a quoted heredoc, rather than fighting apply_diff. This is the same failure family as the pre-existing swarm wiki page `drone-agent-plan-execution-verification-lessons` (lesson 3), which specifically warns against apply_diff on interpolated template lines — it holds for the *surrounding block*, not just the interpolated line itself.

The gateway's `SpawnBackend.sendMessage(session, message): Promise<string>` contract — "wait for the agent's turn and return the reply" — is UNFULFILLABLE in coordinator mode, not merely buggy. The send half is broken (CoordinatorClient posts `/api/messages/relay` with only `{toAgentId, body}`, which 400s at the coordinator route requiring `fromBeaconId`+`fromAgentId`; and even past that, relay lands in the agent's pull-only `pendingMessages` inbox, never a user turn). But the deeper problem is the RECEIVE half: the gateway has NO WebSocket client at all (deps are only drone-core, matrix-js-sdk, pino, better-sqlite3), so it can never observe the agent's reply, which goes to the coordinator event stream. `CoordinatorClient.sendSessionMessage` returns a delivery ACK, not the assistant text. Fixing only the send path would make the surface post the ACK object as the chat reply. Correct split: (1) send-half fix now — deliver via `deliverUserMessage` (WS `{type:'userMessage'}` → `submitUserMessage`), which is the path the coordinator UI already uses, and return `null` = "no synchronous reply" so the surface posts nothing; (2) a separate plan for the receive path (gateway WS subscribe to coordinator `/ws`). Lesson: when a backend method's contract cannot be satisfied by one transport, make the unsatisfiable result EXPLICIT (a nullable return) rather than let a wrong-typed value flow through as if it were the answer.

In the drone-agent repo, `file__apply_diff` has TWO destructive failure modes on large TypeScript files, not one: (1) it collapses/merges hunks whose change zone contains template-literal lines (`` order.push(\`start:${text}\`) ``), swallowing surrounding newlines and a trailing block; (2) it can DUPLICATE the file tail verbatim — appending a stray fragment after the real class close, producing "TS1128: Declaration or statement expected" at the file end. Both were hit this session: `drone-gateway/src/engine.ts` (twice) and `drone-agent/src/runtime/plugin-engine.ts`. Recovery that works: `grep -n '^}' <file>` to find the last genuine top-level close, `head -n <N> <file> > /tmp/x && cp /tmp/x <file>` to truncate, then re-check the build. CRITICAL CAVEAT: the LSP reported these files "clean" while `tsc` failed — trust the BUILD, not LSP, and always run `pnpm --filter <pkg> run build` immediately after editing engine.ts / plugin-engine.ts. Belt-and-suspenders for next time: for any file containing a template literal or that is >300 lines, skip apply_diff entirely and use python (`str.replace` with an exact-count assert) or a heredoc append + head-truncate.

Gateway external-process injection landed on branch feat/gateway-external-process-injection (plan plan-gateway-external-process-injection). New: `controlApi` config (loopback HTTP control API, disabled by default), conversation-level `injection: { enabled: true }` opt-in (loader now keeps a conversation with EITHER non-empty controlSurfaces OR injection.enabled; the wildcard `*` is never an injection target), `GatewayEngine.injectMessage/listAdapterIds/listInjectableConversations` bridge (outbound-only — hands text straight to adapter.sendMessage, bypassing control surfaces AND the per-conversation runOnTail), `src/control-api/server.ts` (Fastify; 404 unknown adapter/conversation, 403 not-opted-in, 400 bad body, optional Bearer token else loopback trust), and a second bin `drone-gateway-inject` with subcommands `inject-message` + `run-agent`. run-agent spawns a local one-shot `drone-agent --once --output-json` (writes `{type:'kickoff',task}` to stdin then closes it; final chat message = LAST assistantMessage; `--no-response-sentinel` suppresses a `<<NO_RESPONSE>>` reply, exit 0). Deferred: coordinator-routed spawn, streaming narration, inbound delivery/continuity. 3672 tests pass.

drone-gateway `LocalSpawnBackend` now drains the child agent's stderr (ADR 238, 2026-10-08). Before: it spawned with `stdio:['pipe','pipe','pipe']` but never read `childProcess.stderr`, so a gateway-spawned agent's stderr was dropped entirely (and the pipe could fill/stall the child) — making the persona-not-found warning invisible. Now it readline-drains stderr into the gateway logger with a bounded ring, and if stdout closes WITHOUT a `turnComplete` the turn returns `Error: agent exited before replying: <stderr tail>` instead of `''` (so the reason reaches chat). The one-shot `inject/spawn-once.ts` helper gets the same treatment: it buffers stderr and includes the tail in `SpawnOnceFailureError` (it previously called `child.stderr.resume()` and discarded the output).

drone-gateway spawn backend is now PER-CONTROL-SURFACE (ADR 238, 2026-10-08). Mode is inferred from the presence/absence of `controlSurfaces[].config.targetBeaconId` (present => coordinator on that beacon; absent => local). `GatewayConfig.spawnBackend` and the gateway-wide `targetBeaconId` are REMOVED; a `config.json` still carrying either is a hard load error. New `SpawnBackendRegistry` (mirrors `SurfaceRegistry`); `GatewayEngine` ctor is now `(config, backends, swarm?)`; `ctx.spawnBackend` stays required and receives the inferred backend. New `src/surfaces/requirements.ts` owns `SPAWNING_SURFACES` (persona-assignment), `SURFACES_REQUIRING_COORDINATOR` (swarm-console), and `resolveSurfaceSpawnMode(spec)`. `coordinatorUrl` is required iff any loaded surface is a coordinator-mode spawner or a swarm-console; one shared `CoordinatorClient` is injected into both `ctx.swarm` and `CoordinatorSpawnBackend`; `createSpawnBackends(config, client?)` replaces `createSpawnBackend`.
